## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anantarapaccayakathā* (Kv 14.3) is the third debate of the fourteenth chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text centers on the doctrinal problem of the continuity of the psychic stream (*santati*) and the functioning of contiguous conditioning (*anantarapaccaya*) [Dube 1980]. In this controversy, the Uttarāpathaka school advocated a strictly unbroken, uninterrupted psychic flow, a stance contested by the Theravādins, who utilized the conceptual distinction between latent (*bhavaṅga*) and manifest or functional (*kiriya*) mental states to explain psychological continuity [Dube 1980].

While SuttaCentral notes no curated historical parallels for the chapter, it records one translation in a modern language [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse (821 matching passages across 47 Pali texts), sharing significant doctrinal formulations with other debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, notably the *Jhānasaṅkantikathā* (Kv 18.6), the preceding *Kusalākusalapaṭisandahanakathā* (Kv 14.1), and debates concerning sense-consciousness and physical phenomena (Kv 6.7–6.10, Kv 10.3–10.5) [DharmaNexus]. Textual segments are also shared with the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 16), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Chachakka Sutta* (MN 148), the *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.3.7) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus identifies conceptual and textual parallels in Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (preserved in Tibetan) and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
